reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes free Amazon and Flipkart gift cards and earnings of up to 1 lakh per month while directing viewers to register through an app with personal details and a referral code. The app links game participation and displayed entry amounts to claims of doubled money or larger winnings, with withdrawal presented as requiring KYC. The records do not establish that any reward was delivered, that a payment succeeded, or what information KYC collects.

opening.argument: The presentation includes conditions and procedural limits that make this a qualified rewards promotion rather than a guarantee of effortless profit. Viewers are told to register, enter a referral code, and complete verification before using the application, while withdrawal is described as requiring KYC. The stated benefits are framed around participation in games and available options, not as an unconditional payment to everyone. The description also presents the offer as an app-based opportunity with a referral code, so a reasonable viewer can understand that eligibility and results depend on following the service's process. Nothing supplied proves that every participant was promised a payout, that payment was impossible, or that the creator concealed the existence of requirements.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opposing account emphasizes the referral link, personal details, and doubled-money language, but those facts establish a promotional app workflow, not deception by themselves. It expressly acknowledges that registration and KYC are required, rather than hiding conditions. Nor does the record show that the creator guaranteed a successful withdrawal or that any viewer lost money. Describing possible game returns is not proof that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: But before that you will have to complete KYC.
Then Go to the withdrawal option and withdraw from here and then you can easily withdraw here.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The requirements do not make the promotion cautious; they identify the steps viewers must take to pursue the promised benefit. The speaker calls the application genuine and says money can be doubled, while the evidence contains no verified payout, no explanation of KYC data use, and no proof that the advertised rewards are available. A disclosed condition can still be part of a deceptive acquisition funnel.

opening.argument: The video's observable format is a hands-on demonstration and tutorial. The speaker walks through sign-up, the application's interface, available games, a sample game, and the route to withdrawal. He specifically introduces the activity as a demonstration and explains how the menus work, including games, contests, referrals, and withdrawal options. The sampled frames likewise show ordinary in-app screens: game choices, a contest interface, ticket selections, and a menu containing “Refer & Earn.” This is instructional coverage of how a service operates, not evidence that the creator fabricated results or impersonated a trusted institution. The source does not establish that the demonstration itself caused a viewer to pay or submit information.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a promotion does not eliminate its tutorial character. The speaker spends substantial time explaining interface functions and showing gameplay, while the supplied frames show actual application screens rather than a fabricated payment receipt or testimonial. The request to subscribe is ordinary channel engagement and does not prove the app claims are fraudulent. The evidence supports a demonstration whose safety and profitability remain unverified.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A tutorial can still be scam promotion when its instructional steps direct viewers into the promoted service. Here, the demonstration is paired with a referral code, a claim that the app is genuine, and claims of doubled money. The frames show interfaces and tickets, but they do not prove a real payout, legitimate odds, or that withdrawal succeeds. Showing a working-looking interface is not evidence that the underlying reward promise is true.

citations.quote: You can enter that referral code in the screen so that you will get this extra benefit.
This application is very genuine
Then Go to the withdrawal option and withdraw from here and then you can easily withdraw here.

opening.argument: The material is also consistent with ordinary promotion of a game-and-rewards service. It shows selectable games, contest entries, tickets, a shop, and a referral feature, all recognizable service functions. Although some entry and winning amounts are discussed, the supplied material does not establish that viewers must deposit money, recruit a downline, surrender passwords, or receive a guaranteed return. The description provides an app link and referral code, which is common in referral marketing, and the speaker explains that KYC precedes withdrawal. Without evidence of an actual failed transaction, credential theft, or concealed mechanism, the record supports a commercial service promotion whose claims may require independent verification, not a proven scam.

citations.quote: For other options, you can refer your friend and you will get some lives.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The evidence does not show the decisive features of a scam mechanism. It does not document a forced deposit, password request, recruitment scheme, or completed loss. The app's visible menus and game choices are compatible with a reward or entertainment service, and the referral feature is disclosed. The opposing account asks the judge to infer fraud from optimistic marketing and uncertainty, but uncertainty about a service is not proof that the service is fraudulent.

citations.quote: For other options, you can refer your friend and you will get some lives.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing evidence does not cure the affirmative claims that are present. The description advertises free gift cards and earnings up to one lakh per month, while the speaker says paid entries can produce doubled amounts and explains how to withdraw. The app requires personal details and KYC, and the record supplies no successful redemption or substantiation for those promises. A scam need not show a password request or completed victim loss in the video.
